proof_summary: The Catalan coefficient sum is rewritten as a binomial-transform sequence \(B_s(N)\) with a period-three weight pattern (the exceptional parameter \(m=-1\) differs only by an additive constant).  Factoring \((1+x)^p-1-x^p=p(1+x+x^2)S\), reciprocal symmetry makes the correction polynomials anti-palindromic, so complementary coefficients pair and a skew-binomial divisibility plus the factorial valuation bound gives \(p^{3e+3}\) (the first two correction terms vanish); Newton interpolation then extends the prime-step congruence from nonnegative to arbitrary integer \(s\).
